name: devin-bundle
description: Devin CLI bundle: skills I use + consolidated rules. Cross-platform installer. Unified and adapted engineering + productivity skill sets.

skills.name: a11y-audit
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to check a frontend for accessibility. Covers keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, color contrast, focus management, and WCAG alignment.

skills.name: afk-loop
skills.purpose: Use when you want the agent to work unattended through local Markdown implementation issues, picking the next ready task from a DAG of blocking relationships.

skills.name: agent-cost-guard
skills.purpose: Use when monitoring token cost per loop, detecting token maxing, or limiting parallel subagents to control cost and context pressure.

skills.name: agent-reach
skills.purpose: Use when researching trends or public sources across credential-free channels (YouTube transcripts/metadata, RSS/Atom feeds). Routes to extensions/agent-reach/wrapper.py, a whitelist passthrough to the agent-reach CLI (`get` grammar)

skills.name: agentic-rag
skills.purpose: Use when implementing an agentic RAG product in a target project (support desk, knowledge assistant, evidence-gated Q&A). Playbook for the retrieve -> decision-gate -> answer-or-escalate architecture with multimodal index and human-review loop. Builds the system; does not answer questions with it.

skills.name: ai-coding-dictionary
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks about AI coding jargon, wants to clarify a term like context engineering, harness engineering, prompt engineering, or agent harness, or when the agent needs to agree on a term definition before continuing a technical discussion.

skills.name: ai-tools
skills.purpose: Use when running local, offline-first ML tooling (mechanistic interpretability PoCs like refusal-direction ablation on local safetensors or the HF cache), when adding self-contained model experiments that print JSON, or when post-training, distilling (s1K/R1-style), or RLVR/GRPO-tuning a reasoning or domain model.

skills.name: ai3d-gen
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks for generative 3D assets (text-to-3D, image-to-3D, mesh synthesis) via self-hosted open models. Routes to extensions/comfyui-operator/wrapper.py against a local ComfyUI server, with direct-model fallbacks (TRELLIS, TripoSG, InstantMesh, Hunyuan3D). All free/open weights, no paid SaaS.

skills.name: animation-direction
skills.purpose: Use when turning narrated video/audio into synced code-rendered motion graphics — narration -> timestamped transcript -> scene plan -> approval gate -> Remotion render -> ffmpeg composite. Covers the motion vocabulary, beat-to-visual mapping, scene-plan v2 schema, and the mandatory plan gate via extensions/asr + extensions/remotion-render.

skills.name: api-context-spec
skills.purpose: Use when generating or maintaining OpenAPI specs as context for AI agents. Ensures API contracts are explicit, versioned, and machine-readable.

skills.name: api-design
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to design, review, or document an API. Covers REST, OpenAPI, versioning, error models, contract testing, and authentication.

skills.name: api-spec
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to design, review, or document an API (REST, OpenAPI, versioning, error models, contract testing, authentication), or when generating/maintaining OpenAPI specs as machine-readable context for AI agents.

skills.name: architecture
skills.purpose: Use when designing modules, seams, and adapters, when evaluating module depth and identifying deepening opportunities in a codebase, or when modernizing legacy code incrementally (strangler-fig, seams, characterization tests, safe extraction).

skills.name: architecture-diagrams
skills.purpose: Use when the deliverable is a physical diagram artifact (.svg/.png) — C4 models, dense class diagrams, network topology rendered via PlantUML. Not for diagrams embedded in Markdown (use Mermaid there).

skills.name: arena
skills.purpose: Use when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape. Spawns N parallel candidates at the same task, cross-judges, picks a base, grafts the strongest parts of the losers into it.

skills.name: ascii-art
skills.purpose: Use when generating animated ASCII art for artifacts the agent produces - README banners (SVG), CLI splash screens, loading/404 states or decorative pieces in web pages and terminals. Wraps the ascii.rest library (217 MIT pieces, React components, npx CLI, image-to-ascii).

skills.name: ask-bundle
skills.purpose: Use when deciding which skill or flow fits your situation — the meta-router entry point for this bundle (direct specialist skills, multi-skill flows, local AFK issues), or when the request is vague and needs the quick-start menu. Routes then defers to the chosen specialist — does not execute the work itself.

skills.name: autonomous-gates
skills.purpose: Use when running long-horizon or multi-step tasks where quality must be verified before proceeding, when the user asks for "autonomous mode" or "run unattended", or when a task has explicit acceptance criteria that must pass before declaring done.

skills.name: benchmark-checklist
skills.purpose: Use when running a benchmark, reporting a measured speedup or regression, or vetting a performance number before acting on it.

skills.name: big-file-refactor
skills.purpose: Use when a source file has grown past roughly 1000 lines, when context compaction is losing track of a file's content, or when asked to break an oversized file into modules safely.

skills.name: binary-triage
skills.purpose: Use when extracting evidence from closed binaries (DLL/SO/EXE/AAR) without heavy RE tooling - engine version, symbols, getter constants, exports, diff between builds, ctypes runtime probing. Answers in minutes what would take hours in Ghidra; escalate to re-binary/Ghidra only when static triage cannot close the question.

skills.name: blast-radius
skills.purpose: Use when asked for the blast radius of a change, what a diff could break elsewhere, or when reviewing a small diff you do not trust. Proves the one safety fact by running real code.

skills.name: brag
skills.purpose: Use when someone says /brag, let's brag about this, make a launch video, turn this into a video, or wants to share what they built. Turns the current project website into a short, polished, shareable launch video using Hyperframes, reading the project code directly with no live URL or screenshots needed.

skills.name: brag-slim
skills.purpose: Use when someone says /brag-slim, let's /brag about this, brag about a website, make a launch video, or wants to show off what they built. Turns a project directory or a website URL into a short, shareable launch video with music, motion, and share copy; one file, no bundled assets, built entirely by the model with the tools already on the machine. If the /brag skill is also installed, let /brag handle those phrases; it hands off here on Opus 5.5.

skills.name: career-ops
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants help running a job hunt end to end: scanning public job boards, scoring role fit, tailoring a CV or cover letter, and tracking applications in a local tracker. The agent never submits applications.

skills.name: cli-adapter
skills.purpose: Use when a tool or app has no MCP server or official connector, when the user asks the agent to control an application, or when a thin CLI wrapper is the cheapest integration path.

skills.name: code-review
skills.purpose: Use when completing a task, reviewing a branch or PR, before merging, when the user asks to 'review since X', when publishing a GitHub PR review with inline comments/suggestions, or when the user receives code review feedback and needs to decide how to act on it.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.purpose: Use when designing modules, seams, adapters, and the structure of a codebase.

skills.name: computer-use
skills.purpose: Use when you need to see or control the local screen (screenshots, screen recording with video + contact sheet for catching transient bugs/animations, mouse clicks/movement, typing text and hotkeys) or to read/control terminals (Windows Terminal, conhost, mintty, spawned PTYs). GUI automation for desktop apps and browsers, replicating Devin Cloud Computer Use in the CLI.

skills.name: context-folding
skills.purpose: Use when context is growing large (approaching model window limits), when long documents or transcripts need to be processed, or when compaction is losing critical information. Adapts Recursive Language Model (RLM) techniques to the Devin CLI runtime.

skills.name: context-hygiene
skills.purpose: Use when context is growing large or the agent forgets earlier instructions, when deciding clear vs compact, when processing documents/logs >50k tokens, when monitoring token cost or limiting subagent fan-out, when choosing a reasoning effort level, or when reducing token/compute/MCP costs. Covers lost-in-the-middle, context folding (RLM), cost guards, and difficulty-matched effort.

skills.name: context-window-hygiene
skills.purpose: Use when a conversation is getting long and the agent seems to be forgetting earlier instructions, before adding MCP servers or rules files, when deciding whether to clear or compact the chat, or when context window budget feels tight. Covers lost-in-the-middle, clear-vs-compact, and lean-context hygiene.

skills.name: context7
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks about a library, framework, or component and up-to-date docs would help.

skills.name: continuous-improvement
skills.purpose: Use when starting a self-improvement session. Enforces FASE 0 deep research and the 10-step improvement loop so no step is skipped, no phantom failure is invented, and every change is validated with held-out tests.

skills.name: correct
skills.purpose: Use when the operator corrects an agent mistake in the repo, or when hardening the project so a repeated agent mistake class cannot happen again.

skills.name: cost-optimization
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to reduce token, compute, or infrastructure costs. Covers context window budget, MCP selection, caching, model routing, and query optimization.

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.purpose: Use when a project needs a scripted way to drive the real app the way a user does and prove behavior, or when asked to make a control/verification skill for the repo. Generates a project-local verify-<app> skill.

skills.name: creative-engineering
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to apply a visual "style", "theme", or "effect" to code — frontend (CSS/GLSL), native shaders, or media processing (Python/OpenCV/FFmpeg) — especially CRT, dither, datamosh, night-vision, brutalist, receipt-print, depth-map, blob/metaball aesthetics. Loads a technical-anatomy knowledge base before writing code.

skills.name: criador-de-devin-app
skills.purpose: Use when turning a recurring intent into a named devin-cli app - a repeatable agent automation with its own name, schedule, prompt and done-when contract. Covers the agentic-app naming framework and the APP.md scaffold.

skills.name: cu-realtime
skills.purpose: Use when computer-use or terminal automation needs the fastest reaction the runtime allows - event waits instead of screenshot polling, text perception instead of image reads, whole perceive-act-verify cycles batched into one exec, or deterministic reflex loops below model latency. Composes with the `computer-use` skill (same extension CLIs).

skills.name: data-analyst
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to query a database, analyze data, create charts/visualizations, explore data patterns, or asks business questions about data. Replicates Devin cloud's Data Analyst Agent (DANA) for the CLI — SQL-first exploration, schema-aware querying, and seaborn-style visualizations via MCP data sources.

skills.name: database
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to design, migrate, query, or optimize a database. Covers schema design, migrations, query review, indexing, and data integrity.

skills.name: de-slop
skills.purpose: Use when cleaning a diff before opening a PR, or when asked to simplify, de-slop, or run the full quality pass on current changes.

skills.name: dead-wire
skills.purpose: Use when running completeness audits, before declaring "it works", or when something looks too implemented to be true. Hunts cut wires: features that look alive but are dead - tables never populated, buttons leading nowhere, events without emitter or listener, flags without write path, request fields the server ignores.

skills.name: debug-ci-failures
skills.purpose: Use when CI is failing and the cause needs to be found across builds, jobs, or environments.

skills.name: debugging
skills.purpose: Use when the user says 'diagnose', 'debug this', reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow, when encountering a bug/test failure/unexpected behavior and a fix is not yet obvious, or when CI is failing and the cause needs to be found across builds, jobs, or environments.

skills.name: deep-mode
skills.purpose: Use when the user says 'deep', 'deep search', 'deep research', 'research this thoroughly', or asks for exhaustive codebase exploration beyond a quick grep. Replicates Ask Devin's Deep Mode (!deep in Slack/Teams) for the CLI - multi-pass agentic search with citations, cross-file synthesis, and architecture mapping.

skills.name: deploy
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to release, deploy, rollback, or verify a deployment pipeline. Covers CI/CD gates, environment checks, canary/blue-green, and post-deploy smoke tests.

skills.name: devin-config
skills.purpose: Use when evolving the agent's capabilities with a new skill, custom subagent, plugin, hook, MCP server, or project rule — or when auditing/managing a project's `.devin/` configuration, producing deterministic read-only reports, detecting broken references/duplicates/divergences, and generating plans that persist under `.devin/` only after approval.

skills.name: devin-manager
skills.purpose: Use when auditing or managing a project's `.devin/` configuration, producing deterministic read-only reports, detecting broken references, duplicates, and divergences, and generating plans that only persist under `.devin/` after explicit approval.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.purpose: Use when the user says 'diagnose', 'debug this', reports something broken, throwing, failing, or slow, or when encountering a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior and a fix is not yet obvious.

skills.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skills.purpose: Use when facing two or more independent tasks with no shared state or ordering, OR when executing a multi-task plan by dispatching a fresh subagent per task.

skills.name: dma
skills.purpose: Use when the user invokes /dma or asks for a pentest, offensive recon, or aggressive audit on an authorized target. Dirty-work pentest agent and recon orchestrator - closes a scope contract with the user, classifies the target type, runs passive/static collection and surface mining, confirms vectors with minimal read-only probes inside the allowlist, and escalates deep testing via web-probe. Every invasive action requires explicit per-batch approval.

skills.name: docker
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to build, run, compose, or deploy containers. Covers Dockerfiles, docker compose, images, volumes, networks, and basic Kubernetes manifests.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.purpose: Use when building or refining a project's domain model, glossary, or bounded contexts.

skills.name: drift-report
skills.purpose: Use when checking whether design documents, READMEs, or specs still match the code they describe. Reads each document, locates the referenced source files, and reports only concrete divergences in a dated drift report. Detection only; does not fix code or docs.

skills.name: e2e-testing
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to add, run, or debug end-to-end tests. Covers Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, happy paths, critical user journeys, and CI integration. Browser-level journeys only; unit/TDD work goes to testing, test infrastructure to observability-quality.

skills.name: edge-cases
skills.purpose: Use when implementing a feature or bugfix, and before declaring done. Enumerate inputs/states/failure modes before coding, defend boundaries while coding, adversarially self-review the diff after. Prevents happy-path-only code.

skills.name: edge-coverage
skills.purpose: Use when assembling or auditing a test suite for rigorous edge-case coverage, when the user asks for meticulous test construction rules, boundary/equivalence analysis, or a completeness standard before a suite may be called done. Extends `testing`, `tdd`, `edge-cases`, and `mutation-testing` with a mandatory Edge Inventory that drives the suite.

skills.name: effort-calibration
skills.purpose: Use when choosing a reasoning effort level for an LLM coding agent, when a task seems to be over-thinking or spending too many tokens, when deciding whether to raise effort, when writing task specifications that substitute for reasoning budget, or when a simple task is being treated as a codebase audit. Covers overthinking, compute-optimal test-time scaling, prompt-induced waste, and difficulty-matched effort.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.purpose: Use when executing a written implementation plan with checkpoints and reviews.

skills.name: execution
skills.purpose: Use when RUNNING an already-written plan/spec/tickets with checkpoints, implementing a feature/fix per spec, deciding how much human review a task needs, or working unattended through local Markdown issues in a blocking DAG (AFK loop). Plans get authored upstream in `planning`/`intake`.

skills.name: fact-check
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to fact-check, tear apart, nitpick, or pre-publish-review an article, essay, blog post, or any markdown/text draft, verifying every checkable claim against online primary sources via adversarial checker subagents. Do not use for code review, security audits, or proofreading without factual verification.

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.purpose: Use when the implementation is complete, all tests pass, and the work needs to be integrated.

skills.name: firmware-probe
skills.purpose: Use when analyzing a declared firmware image or embedded artifact under an engagement contract (extraction, SBOM, CVE mapping, config/credential review). Routes to extensions/offsec-tools/wrapper.py tools: binwalk, unblob, emba; deep RE of extracted binaries goes to re-binary.

skills.name: forensic-debugging
skills.purpose: Use when a bug, algorithm failure, or intermittent defect resists normal debugging, when an audit-grade trail of every hypothesis and experiment is required, or when the user asks for millimetric traceability to localize any failure fast. Extends `debugging` with a mandatory trace ledger, invariant map, and falsification protocol.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.purpose: Use when building new UI or reshaping an existing one and the result must look distinctive and intentional, not templated. Guides aesthetic direction, typography, layout, and copy so the page has a specific point of view for this brief.

skills.name: gates
skills.purpose: Use when about to claim work is complete/fixed/passing, when a task risks agent laziness (large, multi-step, previously half-done, or with acceptance criteria), or when running long-horizon/unattended work where quality must be verified before proceeding. Covers gates, gates ledgers, and autonomous gate semantics. Completion-claim discipline only; writing tests goes to testing or e2e-testing.

skills.name: gh
skills.purpose: Use when interacting with GitHub via the gh CLI from an agent.

skills.name: ghidra
skills.purpose: Use when analyzing raw firmware images (ARM/Thumb embedded), dumped flash, or binaries without symbols - importing at a custom base address, seeding function discovery, and dumping decompiled output + xrefs for offline study via Ghidra headless.

skills.name: git-helper
skills.purpose: Use when managing branches, writing commits, or resolving simple git workflow questions.

skills.name: git-workflows
skills.purpose: Use when managing branches, writing commits, creating isolated worktrees for feature work, or resolving and verifying merge/rebase conflicts.

skills.name: github-actions
skills.purpose: Use when writing or reviewing .github/workflows YAML files or debugging CI. GitHub Actions security and best practices - SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, script injection via PR context, pull_request_target dangers, secrets and OIDC, cache poisoning, matrix and artifacts.

skills.name: grilling
skills.purpose: Use when exploring and stress-testing ideas before committing to a design or plan, when the user says "grill me" or "stress-test this", or when sharpening a plan while also producing ADRs and a glossary.

skills.name: handoff
skills.purpose: Use when the user needs to compact the current conversation into a document for another agent to continue.

skills.name: humanizer
skills.purpose: Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells and rewriting it so it reads like the writer without changing what it says. Covers not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes used everywhere, inflated claims, sales language, stock AI words, bold labels, and filler. Do not use for code, data, or factual verification.

skills.name: hyperframes
skills.purpose: Use when turning HTML/data-attribute animations into MP4 video (kinetic text, web-native motion graphics, DOM-driven scenes). Routes to extensions/hyperframes/wrapper.py, a whitelist passthrough to the hyperframes CLI over npx (Node >= 22 + FFmpeg required).

skills.name: i18n
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to add or review internationalization and localization. Covers locale files, translation keys, pluralization, RTL, and date/number formatting.

skills.name: image-forensics
skills.purpose: Use when checking whether an image is a real camera capture or synthetic/generated, when tagging media provenance before ingestion, when verifying visual evidence for fact-check, or when validating that ai3d-gen source photos are real captures before splatting. Covers PRNU noise-residual forensics, EXIF/XMP/C2PA first pass, and PCE scoring via extensions/image-forensics.

skills.name: impeccable
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks for UI/UX work, wants to fix or polish a page/component, or when an interface looks bland, inconsistent, or like a default template.

skills.name: implement
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to implement a feature or fix from a spec or set of tickets.

skills.name: implement-laya
skills.purpose: Use when a task needs fast typed decisions — classification, triage, scoring, guardrails, moderation, or model routing — over text/JSON states, or when integrating the `laya` engine (non-autoregressive decision model) into a user's codebase.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to evaluate module depth, identify deepening opportunities in a codebase, and act on them.

skills.name: intake
skills.purpose: Use when SIZING a task or PR and deciding whether to split it, validating the "intent" field in tickets/specs/PRDs before implementation, or moving issues and external PRs through triage states (categorise, verify, grill, write agent-ready briefs). Feeds `planning`; does not author plans.

skills.name: intention-capture
skills.purpose: Use when capturing and validating the "intent" field in tickets, specs, or PRDs before implementation. Ensures every task has a clear objective, landing zone, and user impact.

skills.name: jira
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to interact with Jira — search issues, read or update tickets, transition status, add comments, list projects, or run JQL. Routes operations through the Atlassian Rovo MCP server (mcp__atlassian__* tools).

skills.name: knowledge-modeling
skills.purpose: Use when building or refining a project's domain model, glossary, or bounded contexts, when validating tool outputs/data against a domain ontology before side effects, or when extracting entities, relations, evidence, and provenance from Markdown/plain text into a typed versioned knowledge graph under `.devin/`.

skills.name: laya-orchestrator
skills.purpose: Use when a cheap typed check beats reading files into context - batch file classification (contains auth data? has tests?), review risk scoring, or pre-dispatch triage. Laya ranks and abstains, never proves - it is not a substitute for reading primary sources (Rule 12).

skills.name: lean-code
skills.purpose: Use when writing, fixing, refactoring, or reviewing code, choosing dependencies, or when the user asks for the simplest solution, minimal diff, yagni, or complains about over-engineering or bloat.

skills.name: learn-mode
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to own the design while the agent teaches and implements — unfamiliar stacks, junior ramp-up, deliberate-practice sessions. Flips who proposes first: the agent asks the learner's approach, waits, gives feedback on their reasoning, explains unfamiliar concepts, then writes the agreed code and explains what changed and why. Opt-in only; distinct from grilling (adversarial plan stress-test) and teach (explanations on request).

skills.name: legacy-refactor
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to modernize legacy code incrementally. Covers strangler-fig, seams, characterization tests, safe extraction, and risk reduction.

skills.name: leo
skills.purpose: Use when routing and orchestrating any work across this Devin bundle through one universal entry point, including direct specialist skills, multi-skill flows, and local AFK issues.

skills.name: maintain-verification-skill
skills.purpose: Use when keeping a project's verification skill and feature map honest as the app changes. Source-reader fan-out per feature plus one live driving pass; ships at most one PR of proven corrections.

skills.name: mcp-context-audit
skills.purpose: Use when considering adding an MCP server, when context feels bloated with tool definitions, when auditing which MCP servers consume the most context window budget, or before committing a change to mcp_config.json. Estimates per-server tool-definition token cost and flags bloat.

skills.name: mcp-governance
skills.purpose: Use when considering adding an MCP server, when context feels bloated with tool definitions, when auditing which servers consume the most context budget, before committing mcp_config.json changes, or when deciding which servers to keep active per task. Estimates per-server tool-definition token cost and guides lazy enablement.

skills.name: mcp-lazy-enablement
skills.purpose: Use when deciding which MCP servers to keep active, when context feels bloated from unused MCP tools, when a task only needs one MCP server temporarily, or when auditing which servers to enable/disable per task. Guides selective MCP enablement to minimize context-window tax.

skills.name: media-tools
skills.purpose: Use when generating visual artifacts — ASCII art, halftone, dithering, matrix-rain, VHS, pixel-sort, voronoi, and other image/video FX — from images, GIFs, videos, GLB models, or webcam input. Local, offline-first.

skills.name: memory-hygiene
skills.purpose: Use when deciding whether to use cross-session agent memory (MEMORY.md, auto-memory), when auto-memory seems stale or bloated, when preferences leak across unrelated tasks, or when choosing between stateless and memory-equipped operation. Covers memory accumulation, temporal contamination, reasoning drift, and user-authored vs auto-saved preferences.

skills.name: memory-management
skills.purpose: Use when deciding whether to persist knowledge in cross-session agent memory (MEMORY.md, auto-memory), when auto-memory seems stale or preferences leak across tasks, or capturing session outputs worth remembering (answered questions, business rules, conventions, failed approaches). Scope: memory hygiene only — improving skills/rules/hooks belongs to `self-improvement`.

skills.name: mesh-utils
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to inspect, convert, clean, or validate mesh/3D scene files (OBJ, STL, GLB, FBX, USD) via trimesh, PyMeshLab, or pxr. Routes to extensions/mesh-utils/meshops.py. Lightweight stdlib CLI; deps are pip-installed only when needed.

skills.name: mobile-probe
skills.purpose: Use when assessing a declared Android or iOS application under an engagement contract (static analysis, decompilation, runtime instrumentation on emulators/devices). Routes to extensions/offsec-tools/wrapper.py tools: jadx, apktool, mobsf, frida, objection. Methodology per OWASP MASVS/MASTG.

skills.name: mutation-testing
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to find testing gaps, mutation test, or identify surviving mutants.

skills.name: net-probe
skills.purpose: Use when probing declared hosts or networks under an engagement contract (port/service scan, SMB/AD enumeration, TLS audit, vulnerability scan). Routes to extensions/offsec-tools/wrapper.py tools: nmap, masscan, netexec, enum4linux-ng, testssl.sh, openvas. Verify-not-exploit by default.

skills.name: no-comments
skills.purpose: Use when hunting comment smells, workaround comments, or stale suppressions on a diff, or when asked to delete comments and encode claimed constraints before a PR.

skills.name: observability-quality
skills.purpose: Use when adding logging, metrics, distributed tracing, error monitoring, linting, architecture testing, or test infrastructure to a project. Covers OpenTelemetry, Sentry/Datadog/Grafana, Biome/ESLint, ArchUnit, commitlint, Knip, Playwright, and coverage strategy. Infrastructure and tooling quality only; writing feature tests goes to testing or e2e-testing.

skills.name: obsidian-workflow

skills.name: ontology-validator
skills.purpose: Use when validating tool outputs or data against a domain ontology or structured knowledge base. Ensures entities, types, and relations are consistent before side effects.

skills.name: operate-blender

skills.name: operate-godot
skills.purpose: Use when the user asks to build, inspect, import assets into, or export a Godot 4 project headlessly (realtime 3D delivery, game scenes, interactive world execution). Uses godot --headless --script CLI; no GUI. Free/MIT engine.

skills.name: operate-spline

Routes to extensions/spline-operator/wrapper.py, which speaks the app's embedded MCP bridge (ws://127.0.0.1:19692) - structured tool calls, not GUI clicking.

skills.name: performance
skills.purpose: Use when the user wants to profile, optimize, load-test, or measure the performance of code, queries, or infrastructure.
